To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the genetic influences on posttraumatic stress symptoms in combat veterans were similar to the genetic influences on PTSD in noncombat populations, but the environmental influences on combat-related PTSD were unique.

1) PTSD is heritable, 2) PTSD is associated with a genetic predisposition for anxiety and depression, 3) PTSD is associated to a lesser degree with a genetic predispo-sition for substance dependence, 4) a history of trauma is the primary environmental factor that increases the risk for PTSD, and 5) PTSD is associated, to varying degrees, with a genetic predis-position for other psychiatric disorders.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the relationship between neurobiological factors and the development of PTSD in a large population-based sample of combat-exposed male twins.
the role of neurologic vulnerability factors in combat-related posttrauma psychiatric disorders.
the role of subtle neurologic compromise as an important vulnerability factor in the etiology of combat-related PTSD.
